title: wish + Past Simple - desire to change the present
shortExplanation: I wish I knew the answer. I wish I had more time.
longExplanation:
wish + Past Simple - about an unrealistic desire in the present.
The form is the same as in the 2nd type of conditional. For to be - were (formally), although was is also used.
formation: I wish I knew the answer. I wish I had more time.

examples.sentence: I wish I spoke better English.
examples.translation: It's a pity that I don't speak English better.

examples.sentence: She wishes she lived in a warmer country.
examples.translation: She would like to live in a warmer country.

title: wish + Past Perfect - regret about the past
shortExplanation: I wish I had studied harder. I wish I hadn't said that.
longExplanation: wish + Past Perfect - regret about past events that cannot be changed. The form is as in the 3rd type of conditional.
formation: I wish I had studied harder. I wish I hadn't said that.

examples.sentence: I wish I hadn't eaten so much.
examples.translation: It's a shame I ate so much.

examples.sentence: She wishes she had taken that job offer.
examples.translation: She wishes she had accepted that job offer.

title: wish + would - desire to change someone else's behavior
shortExplanation: I wish you would stop talking. I wish it would warm up.
longExplanation: wish + would - irritation due to someone else's behavior or a desire to change the situation.
formation: I wish you would stop talking. I wish it would warm up.

examples.sentence: I wish you would listen to me.
examples.translation: I wish you would listen to me.

examples.sentence: I wish it would stop raining.
examples.translation: I wish the rain would stop.

title: Defining vs non-defining clauses
shortExplanation: The man who called (determines which one) vs My brother, who called, (adds info)
longExplanation:
Defining (defining): without commas - they clarify who/what they are talking about. The pronoun can be replaced with that. It cannot be removed without losing the meaning.
Non-defining: with commas - add information without changing the meaning. That cannot be used. Can be removed.
formation: The man who called (determines which one) vs My brother, who called, (adds info)

examples.sentence: The film that I told you about is on tonight. (какой именно)
examples.translation: The movie I told you about is showing tonight.

examples.sentence: My sister, who lives in Paris, is visiting next week. (доп. инфо)
examples.translation: My sister, who lives in Paris, will arrive next week.

title: Prepositions in relative clauses
shortExplanation: the person I work with / the person with whom I work (formally)
longExplanation:
In colloquial speech, the preposition comes at the end: the house I grew up in.
In written/formal speech, the preposition before which/whom: the house in which I grew up.
After the preposition - only which (for things) and whom (for people). Never that!
formation: the person I work with / the person with whom I work (formally)

examples.sentence: The project I'm working on is fascinating. (разг.)
examples.translation: The project I'm working on is very interesting.

examples.sentence: The project on which I am working is fascinating. (форм.)

title: Consequence conjunctions: so... that, such... that, therefore, as a result
shortExplanation: It was so cold that we stayed inside. She worked hard; therefore, she passed.
longExplanation:
so + adjective/adverb + that: He spoke so quickly that nobody understood.
such + (a/an) + adjective + noun + that: It was such a long film that I fell asleep.
Connecting words of result (between sentences): therefore, consequently, as a result, hence, thus.
formation: It was so cold that we stayed inside. She worked hard; therefore, she passed.

examples.sentence: It was such a good book that I read it twice.
examples.translation: The book was so good that I read it twice.

examples.sentence: She missed the deadline; consequently, she lost the contract.
examples.translation: She missed the deadline; As a result, she lost her contract.

pattern: be used to / get used to + V-ing
title: be used to / get used to + V-ing - habit (real)
shortExplanation: I'm used to waking up early. She's getting used to the cold.
longExplanation:
be used to + V-ing / noun = to be used to (already used to).
get used to + V-ing / noun = get used to (the process of getting used to).
• I used to live in Paris. - used to live (no longer)
• I am used to living in big cities. - used to living in big cities
formation: I'm used to waking up early. She's getting used to the cold.

examples.sentence: I'm not used to getting up so early.
examples.translation: I'm not used to getting up so early.

examples.sentence: It took time, but she got used to the new system.
examples.translation: It took time, but she got used to the new system.

title: Future in the Past: would / was going to
shortExplanation: She said she would call. He was going to leave.
longExplanation:
Future in the Past - constructions that express the future from the point of view of the past. Used in indirect speech and narrative.
• would + V (from will): She said she would come.
• was/were going to + V: He was going to call but forgot.
• was about to + V: She was about to leave when he arrived.
formation: She said she would call. He was going to leave.

examples.sentence: She promised she would be there.
examples.translation: She promised that she would come.

examples.sentence: He was about to leave when she called.
examples.translation: He was about to leave when she called.

title: be to - official appointment and order
shortExplanation: You are to report by Monday. They were never to meet again.
longExplanation:
be to + infinitive - official orders, planned events and fate in the narrative.
1. Legal Instruction: Passengers are to remain seated.
2. Official plan: The summit is to take place next month.
3. Fate in the narrative: They were never to meet again.
formation: You are to report by Monday. They were never to meet again.

examples.sentence: You are to submit the report by Friday.
examples.translation: You must submit your report by Friday.

examples.sentence: She was to become one of the greatest scientists of her time.
examples.translation: She was destined to become one of the greatest scientists.

title: ought to - moral duty and logical expectation
shortExplanation: You ought to apologise. She ought to have told us.
longExplanation:
ought to is a moral obligation or logical expectation. Stronger should.
Always with to: ought to go (as opposed to should).
For the past: ought to have + V3 - reproach or regret.
formation: You ought to apologise. She ought to have told us.

examples.sentence: You ought to apologise for what you said.
examples.translation: You should apologize for what you said.

examples.sentence: She ought to have told us earlier.
examples.translation: She should have told us sooner.

title: need - modal and regular verb
shortExplanation: You needn't worry. / She doesn't need to come.
longExplanation:
need as a modal (formal, in questions/negations) and as a regular verb.
Modal (without -s, without to):
• You needn't worry. / Need I explain?
Regular need + to:
• She doesn't need to come.
formation: You needn't worry. / She doesn't need to come.

examples.sentence: You needn't fill in both forms.
examples.translation: You do not need to fill out both forms.

examples.sentence: She doesn't need to attend every meeting.
examples.translation: She does not have to attend every meeting.

title: dare - courage and challenge
shortExplanation: How dare you! I daren't ask. She dared to challenge him.
longExplanation:
dare - dare, dare. Modal in rhetorical questions and negations.
Modal: How dare you! / I daren't ask. / Dare I say...
Normal: She didn't dare to look. / He dared to challenge the boss.
formation: How dare you! I daren't ask. She dared to challenge him.

examples.sentence: How dare you speak to me like that!
examples.translation: How dare you talk to me like that!

examples.sentence: She dared to express her opinion openly.
examples.translation: She dared to openly express her opinion.

title: Reflexive pronouns: myself, yourself, himself...
shortExplanation: I hurt myself. She did it herself. They enjoyed themselves.
longExplanation:
myself, yourself, yourself, yourself, yourself, yourself, yourselves, yourself.
1. The action is directed towards the subject: He cut himself.
2. Emphase (by yourself, without help): I did it myself.
Stable: by myself = alone; help yourself = help yourself.
formation: I hurt myself. She did it herself. They enjoyed themselves.

examples.sentence: She taught herself to play the guitar.
examples.translation: She taught herself to play the guitar.

examples.sentence: The machine turns itself off automatically.
examples.translation: The machine turns off automatically.

title: Collective nouns: team, family, committee...
shortExplanation: The team are playing well. (BrE) / The team is playing. (AmE)
longExplanation:
Collective nouns are a group as a whole.
• BrE: usually plural. number: The team are playing.
• AmE: usually units. number: The team is playing.
Frequent: team, family, government, committee, staff, audience, crew, police, army, public, management
formation: The team are playing well. (BrE) / The team is playing. (AmE)

examples.sentence: The government have announced new measures. (BrE)
examples.translation: The government announced new measures.

examples.sentence: The audience were on their feet. (BrE)
examples.translation: The audience jumped to their feet.

title: Fractions and mathematics
shortExplanation: a half, three quarters, 5.7 = five point seven, 25%
longExplanation:
Fractions:½ = a half; ⅓ = a third; ¼ = a quarter; ¾ = three quarters; ⅔ = two thirds.
Numerator is quantitative, denominator is ordinal (plural if numerator > 1).
Decimals: period (not comma): 3.14 = three point one four.
Mathematics: + = plus; - = minus; × = times; ÷ = divided by; = = equals.
formation: a half, three quarters, 5.7 = five point seven, 25%

examples.sentence: Three quarters of students passed the exam.
examples.translation: Three quarters of the students passed the exam.

examples.sentence: The inflation rate fell to 2.5 percent.
examples.translation: The inflation rate dropped to 2.5 percent.
